A regime insider says the Islamic Republic does not need nuclear weapons to destroy Israel and can make it uninhabitable with radioactive dirty weapons.

Hamzeh Rahim-Safavi declared that if the Islamic Republic is not allowed to survive, Israel will not survive either. He pointed to “all kinds of dirty bombs” that require less sophisticated technology than a conventional nuclear weapon.

When the discussion turned to placing enriched uranium inside missile warheads, Safavi said such a weapon could produce a similar result. He also questioned whether anyone could guarantee that the regime possesses only the enriched uranium it has officially declared.

Safavi is the son of Yahya Rahim-Safavi, a former IRGC commander-in-chief and longtime military adviser to the supreme leadership. He is also a University of Tehran faculty member who regularly appears in regime-aligned discussions about deterrence and national security.

This is not ordinary deterrence language.

Safavi is normalizing radioactive contamination as a weapon for preserving clerical rule. He is effectively arguing that if the Islamic Republic faces destruction, it should make another country uninhabitable rather than accept its own defeat.

A radiological dirty bomb is not the same as a nuclear weapon. It uses conventional explosives to disperse radioactive material rather than producing a nuclear explosion. It could contaminate populated areas, trigger mass panic and evacuation, and inflict enormous long-term economic damage.

That distinction does not make the threat less serious. It means the technological barrier could be considerably lower.

The most revealing part of Safavi’s statement is that he tied the threat to the survival of the Islamic Republic, not the Iranian people.

The regime routinely treats Iran, its population and its clerical system as though they were the same thing. They are not. Iran can survive the Islamic Republic. The Islamic Republic cannot survive without holding Iran hostage.

A regime willing to massacre its own people to preserve power is now openly discussing the mass contamination of another people. Its record of slaughter inside Iran makes its threats of an atrocity against Israel impossible to dismiss as empty rhetoric. The world cannot wait for Holocaust-scale violence before taking eliminationist threats seriously.

This threat cannot be separated from the regime’s broader strategy. Its leaders have spent decades calling for Israel’s elimination while developing enrichment capacity, long-range missiles and a proxy network capable of attacking from several fronts.

A nuclear or radiological capability would not exist separately from that strategy. It would shield and strengthen it.

The regime could intensify proxy warfare, attack regional infrastructure and disrupt the Persian Gulf while calculating that the threat of unconventional retaliation would deter direct action against it.

Its ideological structure makes this even more dangerous. The IRGC is not a conventional national military. It is an ideological force built to defend clerical rule, export the revolution and pursue a religious mission extending beyond Iran’s borders.

Not every official welcomes catastrophic war, and the leadership has repeatedly demonstrated a powerful instinct for self-preservation. Safavi’s statement does not prove that the Islamic Republic currently possesses a dirty bomb or has issued an operational order to use one.

This is not independent media reporting neutrally on an American election. It is regime-affiliated media promoting the candidate it considers most useful to its interests.

Sazandegi represents the regime’s so-called reformist and centrist wing, but the division from hardliners is tactical, not foundational. Both operate inside the same anti-American system, accept the Supreme Leader’s authority and work to preserve clerical rule.

The reformist-hardliner rivalry is largely managed political theatre within one regime.

Hardliners threaten the United States openly. Reformists seek agreements, sanctions relief and Western political allies who will reduce pressure. Their language and methods differ, but both protect the Islamic Republic and its revolutionary system.

That is why Sazandegi is promoting El-Sayed.

El-Sayed opposes the American war with Iran, attacks Trump’s foreign policy, criticizes Israel and AIPAC, and favours the approach most likely to reduce military and economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.

He has also refused to clearly condemn the Islamic Republic and the IRGC when pressed, even as the regime’s security forces massacre protesters, plot assassinations abroad and threaten American interests.

That makes him valuable to the regime even if he does not formally support it.

NIAC Action endorsed Mamdani and has supported El-Sayed alongside progressive politicians such as Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, Ro Khanna and Ayanna Pressley. Iranian-American Representative Yassamin Ansari received similar front-page treatment after attacking Trump’s Iran policy and rejecting externally supported regime change. She has described the Islamic Republic as brutal, but her opposition to decisive external pressure still serves its immediate survival interests.

The regime has followed this strategy for years.

The Islamic Republic sees Abdul El-Sayed as useful against Trump, maximum pressure and those seeking to hold the regime accountable. That is why its supposedly reformist media is presenting him as “Trump’s Nightmare.” https://t.co/aPkv58qVy2

outsiders.name: The Iran Watcher
outsiders.hook:
A regime insider says the Islamic Republic does not need nuclear weapons to destroy Israel and can make it uninhabitable with radioactive dirty weapons.

Hamzeh Rahim-Safavi declared that if the Islamic Republic is not allowed to survive, Israel will not survive either. He pointed to “all kinds of dirty bombs” that require less sophisticated technology than a conventional nuclear weapon.

When the discussion turned to placing enriched uranium inside missile warheads, Safavi said such a weapon could produce a similar result. He also questioned whether anyone could guarantee that the regime possesses only the enriched uranium it has officially declared.

Safavi is the son of Yahya Rahim-Safavi, a former IRGC commander-in-chief and longtime military adviser to the supreme leadership. He is also a University of Tehran faculty member who regularly appears in regime-aligned discussions about deterrence and national security.

This is not ordinary deterrence language.

Safavi is normalizing radioactive contamination as a weapon for preserving clerical rule. He is effectively arguing that if the Islamic Republic faces destruction, it should make another country uninhabitable rather than accept its own defeat.

A radiological dirty bomb is not the same as a nuclear weapon. It uses conventional explosives to disperse radioactive material rather than producing a nuclear explosion. It could contaminate populated areas, trigger mass panic and evacuation, and inflict enormous long-term economic damage.

That distinction does not make the threat less serious. It means the technological barrier could be considerably lower.

The most revealing part of Safavi’s statement is that he tied the threat to the survival of the Islamic Republic, not the Iranian people.

The regime routinely treats Iran, its population and its clerical system as though they were the same thing. They are not. Iran can survive the Islamic Republic. The Islamic Republic cannot survive without holding Iran hostage.

A regime willing to massacre its own people to preserve power is now openly discussing the mass contamination of another people. Its record of slaughter inside Iran makes its threats of an atrocity against Israel impossible to dismiss as empty rhetoric. The world cannot wait for Holocaust-scale violence before taking eliminationist threats seriously.

This threat cannot be separated from the regime’s broader strategy. Its leaders have spent decades calling for Israel’s elimination while developing enrichment capacity, long-range missiles and a proxy network capable of attacking from several fronts.

A nuclear or radiological capability would not exist separately from that strategy. It would shield and strengthen it.

The regime could intensify proxy warfare, attack regional infrastructure and disrupt the Persian Gulf while calculating that the threat of unconventional retaliation would deter direct action against it.

Its ideological structure makes this even more dangerous. The IRGC is not a conventional national military. It is an ideological force built to defend clerical rule, export the revolution and pursue a religious mission extending beyond Iran’s borders.

Hardline elements also frame confrontation with Israel and the United States through Mahdist and apocalyptic language. Not every official welcomes catastrophic war, and the leadership has repeatedly demonstrated a powerful instinct for self-preservation. But no responsible security policy can ignore a political culture that glorifies martyrdom and presents regional confrontation as a civilizational duty.

Safavi’s statement does not prove that the Islamic Republic currently possesses a dirty bomb or has issued an operational order to use one.

It does prove that regime-connected figures are publicly discussing radioactive warfare as an acceptable fallback if the conventional nuclear-bomb project remains incomplete.

The Islamic Republic is not merely seeking deterrence to protect Iran. Its insiders are openly threatening mass contamination and mutual destruction to preserve the regime itself. https://t.co/YG4PKXFenv

outsiders.hook:
The Islamic Republic has endorsed Abdul El-Sayed, touting his anti-Americanism and opposition to Trump.

Sazandegi, the newspaper of the Executives of Construction Party inside the Islamic Republic’s political system, placed the Michigan Senate candidate prominently on its front page under the headline “Trump’s Nightmare.”

This is not independent media reporting neutrally on an American election. It is regime-affiliated media promoting the candidate it considers most useful to its interests.

Sazandegi represents the regime’s so-called reformist and centrist wing, but the division from hardliners is tactical, not foundational. Both operate inside the same anti-American system, accept the Supreme Leader’s authority and work to preserve clerical rule.

The reformist-hardliner rivalry is largely managed political theatre within one regime.

Hardliners threaten the United States openly. Reformists seek agreements, sanctions relief and Western political allies who will reduce pressure. Their language and methods differ, but both protect the Islamic Republic and its revolutionary system.

That is why Sazandegi is promoting El-Sayed.

El-Sayed opposes the American war with Iran, attacks Trump’s foreign policy, criticizes Israel and AIPAC, and favours the approach most likely to reduce military and economic pressure on the Islamic Republic.

He has also refused to clearly condemn the Islamic Republic and the IRGC when pressed, even as the regime’s security forces massacre protesters, plot assassinations abroad and threaten American interests.

That makes him valuable to the regime even if he does not formally support it.

The Islamic Republic does not require Western politicians to praise its repression. It benefits when they condemn war and sanctions while refusing to confront the system responsible for the nuclear crisis, proxy warfare and mass killing inside Iran.

The same pattern appeared with Zohran Mamdani. Regime media celebrated his victory as a defeat for Trump, Israel and the American political establishment. Some outlets framed it as evidence of Western decline and the growing reach of the Islamic Revolution’s political narrative.

شاهزاده رضا پهلوی هم‌زمان با ورود به بروکسل برای دیدار با رهبران اروپایی،با انتشار پیامی درباره اعدام دو تن دیگر از معترضان خیزش ۱۸ و ۱۹دی،خواستار پایان سیاست مماشات اروپا با جمهوری اسلامی و حمایت از مردم ایران برای سرنگونی این رژیم شد.

شاهزاده رضا پهلوی در پایان پیام خود تأکید کرد:«اکنون زمان شجاعت اخلاقی و روشن‌بینی راهبردی است،زمان آن رسیده که به مردم ایران برای پایان دادن به این رژیم وحشت و سرکوب یاری رسانده شود.»
